items.title: convert : add DeepSeek V4.1 (DeepseekV41ForCausalLM)
items.body:
## Overview

Adds conversion support for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM`) by subclassing the existing V4 model, under its own `deepseek41` architecture. Most of the V4 path carries over unchanged.

Differences that needed handling:

- Text parameters are nested under `text_config`, so they are promoted in `index_tensors`. Overriding `load_hparams` does not work, because `ModelBase.__init__` calls it explicitly rather than through the instance.
- `num_hash_layers` is absent in V4.1 while the V4 path reads it unconditionally.
- The FP8 scale block size is `[32, 32]` rather than `[128, 128]`. V4 hardcodes 128, and reusing that value rescales every dequantized weight without raising, so the block size is now read from `quantization_config`.
- Indexer `k_norm` and `wk` map onto the existing `INDEXER_K_NORM` and `INDEXER_ATTN_K`. `attn.compressor.ape` and `attn.indexer.compressor.*` are absent in V4.1 and go unused.
- Four new tensors for the engram conditional memory.

The two engram tables need a separate write path. Each is `384,006,168 x 256`, and the inherited FP8 dequant computes `weight.float() * scale` over the whole tensor, which is about 393 GB as float32 for one table. They are read in row blocks from the safetensors shard, quantized per block, and accumulated into a disk backed memmap. Their scale layout also differs: `[rows, 8]`, one scale per 32 columns of a single row, rather than the `[rows/32, cols/32]` tiling the linear weights use.

## The architecture name

An earlier revision of this PR rode on `MODEL_ARCH.DEEPSEEK4` and added the engram tensors to V4's own list. That was wrong twice over, and it now declares `deepseek41` instead. `DEEPSEEK4` is left untouched.

**Convention.** llama.cpp does not mirror the HF `model_type`, it drops the `_v`: `deepseek_v2` became `deepseek2`, `deepseek_v3.2` became `deepseek32`, `qwen2_moe` became `qwen2moe`. Only 10 of the 150 arch strings in `constants.py` contain an underscore at all, so vLLM's `deepseek_v41` would be the odd one out here.

**Correctness.** V4.1 emits `attn_kv_a_norm`, which `DEEPSEEK4`'s declared tensor list does not contain, so the old output did not conform to the architecture it claimed.

**Failure mode.** V4.1 ships the per-layer `hc_attn_{fn,base,scale}` and `hc_ffn_{fn,base,scale}`, 40 of each, but none of `output_hc_fn`, `output_hc_base` or `output_hc_scale`. Routing a V4.1 file to the V4 loader therefore produces a confusing partial match rather than a clean refusal.

`deepseek41`'s tensor list is the 39 families the converter actually writes, derived by reverse mapping them through `TENSOR_NAMES` rather than by trimming V4's list. Against `DEEPSEEK4` it drops `HC_HEAD_{FN,BASE,SCALE}`, `FFN_GATE_TID2EID`, `ATTN_KV_NORM`, `ATTN_COMPRESSOR_APE`, `INDEXER_COMPRESSOR_*` and all six `NEXTN_*`, and adds the four engram entries plus `ATTN_KV_A_NORM`.

Draft, because this is the conversion half only. There is no `deepseek41` runtime yet, so a converted file does not load. Posting it now so the tensor naming can be looked at before more files are produced against it.

## Additional information

Converted `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` end to end on one machine with 121 GiB of RAM: 1046 tensors, 507.9 GB at `--outtype q8_0` with MXFP4 experts, peak host memory under 8 GB above baseline. Output checked with `GGUFReader`, all 8 engram tensors present. Quantized further to Q2_K and Q3_K_M to confirm the file is well formed downstream. `Q2_K_S` and `IQ2_M` both report that they need an imatrix, which is not obtainable until the model runs.

Measured rung sizes, for anyone estimating: Q8_0 staging 473.1 GiB (1046 tensors), Q2_K 246.3 GiB, Q3_K_M 323.4 GiB. Those ratios read high against the staging file because it is not uniformly Q8_0: routed experts land as MXFP4, so parts of the ladder move up rather than down. At Q3_K_M the expert down projection goes MXFP4 to q5_K and grows from 2295 to 2970 MiB.
